**Structure** (or **form**) is how a piece is built from sections. Sections are named with letters: the first idea is
**A**, a different one **B**, the next new one **C**. When A comes back it keeps its letter.

## 1. Phrases and sections

A **phrase** is a musical sentence, usually 2, 4 or 8 [measures]{.nn}, ending in a [cadence](elements-harmony.qmd#cadences).
Phrases join into **sections**. To find the sections, listen for where the music *changes*: a new tune, a new key, new
instruments, a new texture or a different mood.

## 2. Binary form: A B

Two sections. B contrasts with A in some way (a new key, a new tune), and usually **both are repeated**: A A B B.
Common in Baroque dances.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="110"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Binary: A (repeated) moves to the dominant, B (repeated) comes home
M:3/4
L:1/4
K:G
|:"^A""G"G B d|"D7"c A F|"G"G B d|"D"A3|"G"B G B|"Am"c A c|"D"d2 ^c|"D"d3:|
|:"^B""D"d f a|"G"g e c|"D"A d f|"A"e3|"D"f d B|"D7"c A F|"D"A2 F|"G"G3:|]
</script></div>

## 3. Ternary form: A B A

Three sections: A, a contrasting B, then A again. The return can be exact or slightly changed (A B A′).

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Ternary: A in C major, B in A minor, A again
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
"^A""C"E G c G|"F"A F "G"D B,|"C"E G c G|"G"D B, "C"C2|
"^B""Am"A, C E A|"Dm"F D "E"E ^G,|"Am"A, C E A|"E"^G, B, "Am"A,2|
"^A""C"E G c G|"F"A F "G"D B,|"C"E G c G|"G"D B, "C"C2|]
</script></div>

## 4. Rondo form: A B A C A

The opening section, the **refrain**, keeps coming back, with contrasting sections called **episodes** in between.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="120"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Rondo: A B A C A
M:2/4
L:1/8
K:F
"^A""F"c2 A2|"C"G2 E2|"F"F A c f|"C"e2 "F"f2|
"^B""Dm"d2 f2|"Gm"g2 B2|"A"^c e a g|"Dm"f2 d2|
"^A""F"c2 A2|"C"G2 E2|"F"F A c f|"C"e2 "F"f2|
"^C""Bb"B,2 D2|"F"F2 A2|"C"G E C E|"F"F4|
"^A""F"c2 A2|"C"G2 E2|"F"F A c f|"C"e2 "F"f2|]
</script></div>

## 5. Strophic form: A A A

The same music for every **verse** (every *strophe*), with new words each time. Hymns, folk songs, ballads and many
children's songs.

When the music *never* repeats and keeps changing to follow the words or the story, the opposite of strophic, it is
**through-composed**.

## 6. Minuet and trio

A **minuet** is a dance in 3/4 at a moderate tempo, from 17th- and 18th-century Europe. In the Classical period it was
paired with a second, contrasting minuet called the **trio** (once played by just three instruments). Each is in binary
form; then the minuet comes back without its repeats. Overall it is ternary:

| Minuet | Trio | Minuet |
|---|---|---|
| A (repeated) B (repeated) | C (repeated) D (repeated) | A B (no repeats) |
| tonic key | a related key, lighter or thinner scoring | tonic key |

## 7. Popular song forms

| Form | Sections |
|---|---|
| **Verse–chorus** | intro, verse, chorus, verse, chorus, bridge, chorus, outro |
| **AABA (32-bar song)** | A A B A, each 8 [measures]{.nn}; B is the *bridge* or *middle eight* |
| **12-bar blues** | the same 12-[measure]{.nn} chord pattern, repeated ([Blues Changes](blues-changes.qmd)) |
| **Theme and variations** | a tune, then changed versions of it (new rhythm, harmony, key, instruments) |

Naming the parts of a song and marking them in a recording: [Section Labels](section-labels.qmd).
